review_notes: Read the whole file and checked Mathlib for an existing ring-equivalence regularity-transfer lemma (only Equiv.isSMulRegular_congr exists; no IsRegular-via-RingEquiv/AlgEquiv lemma found). The main repeated reasoning is the regularity transport through the variable-selecting equivalence in the two relation lemmas. The separate duplicated Algebra/Module setup in rncMap_flat_iff is mostly instance plumbing, so I did not report it. The degree-one and Hankel-minor parts are not repeated. The proposed lemma has not been compiled. The scalar-action convention for the multiplication-on-self SMul instances should be checked when it is written.

findings.excerpt:
have hleft : IsLeftRegular p :=
      (Equiv.isSMulRegular_congr (e := e.toEquiv) (r := p) (s := e p)
        (fun q => e.map_mul p q)).mpr hregular.left
    exact ⟨hleft, hleft.right_of_commute (fun q => mul_comm p q)⟩
findings.problem: Both relation lemmas end with the same non-trivial argument. A regularity statement for `e p` in the polynomial ring `Polynomial (MvPolynomial _ R)` is pulled back along an algebra equivalence `e`. It goes through `Equiv.isSMulRegular_congr`, `e.map_mul` and `hregular.left`. Left regularity is then upgraded to two-sided regularity using commutativity. The block is copied verbatim at lines 75–78 and 114–117. Only the equivalence `e` and the element `p` differ. Each copy needs the same awkward `(e := e.toEquiv) (r := p) (s := e p)` instantiation. The file also never states the intermediate fact, 'regular after a ring/algebra equivalence implies regular before it', so a reader has to re-derive it each time.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a private lemma before the two relation lemmas, for example
`private theorem isRegular_of_algEquiv_apply {R A B : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] (e : A ≃ₐ[R] B) {p : A} (h : IsRegular (e p)) : IsRegular p`.
Proof sketch: take the block from lines 75–78 verbatim, with `hregular` replaced by `h`. That is `have hleft : IsLeftRegular p := (Equiv.isSMulRegular_congr (e := e.toEquiv) (r := p) (s := e p) (fun q => e.map_mul p q)).mpr h.left`, then `exact ⟨hleft, hleft.right_of_commute (fun q => mul_comm p q)⟩`. Commutativity of `A` is what makes `mul_comm` available.
Then the two uses shrink. In `degree_zero_regular_relation`, `exact isRegular_of_algEquiv_apply (MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv R 0) hregular`. In `quadratic_regular_relation`, `exact isRegular_of_algEquiv_apply e hregular`. The `let p`/`let e` setup and the `hregular` computations are unchanged. The only requirement is that `p` and `e` are definitionally the ones already in scope.
findings.benefit: Removes two copies of the transport proof. The generic statement is named and documented once, so each relation lemma only has to show the polynomial's image under its chosen variable-selecting equivalence is monic-regular. A later change, such as a Mathlib lemma replacing the proof, is made in one place.
